artworks.title: Monumental aquamarine scavo corroso vase
artworks.summary: A large, heavy vase in aquamarine glass with a matt scavo surface, two applied ring handles and an undulating relief around the body. It carries a Seguso Arte Vetro factory label.
description: The rounded body rises into a tall cylindrical neck. Two ring handles of colourless glass are applied on either side of the neck, and a broad undulating relief runs all the way around the lower body. The vase is 32 cm high and 30 cm wide and weighs 7.5 kg, which is heavy for its size.

The surface is matt and finely granular throughout: a scavo finish, which imitates the weathered skin of glass recovered from the ground. The aquamarine colour varies from light turquoise to grey-green and a deeper green, with paler and darker patches. The foot is ground flat and is smoother than the rest of the surface. No engraved signature has been found.

A printed factory label on the lower body reads MURANO ITALY, SEGUSO, arte vetro, around a large stylised S. It is the main evidence for the maker, Seguso Arte Vetro, also known as Seguso AV. That firm should not be confused with Seguso Vetri d'Arte, a different Murano glassworks with its own history and archive.

Auction and reference sources connect Seguso Arte Vetro with the Murano glass artist Livio Seguso (born on Murano in 1930). Dealers have offered closely related vases in aquamarine and in white; the seller of the white example describes it as designed by Livio Seguso and made by Bisazza Vetro in 1993 (see Comparable examples). That makes a link with his designs plausible, but it does not show that he designed this vase. The model, designer and date of this example are still being researched.

marks.location: lower body, just above the foot
marks.observation: Printed factory label with white lettering on a transparent ground, so the glass shows through. MURANO and ITALY run upwards along the left edge; a large stylised S is followed by E / GU / SO, with 'arte vetro' below.
marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the photograph. The S of SEGUSO is the large initial; the remaining letters are stacked as E / GU / SO.
marks.interpretation: Factory label of Seguso Arte Vetro (Seguso AV), Murano. The period in which this label was used has not been established.

assertions.publicNote: Based on the printed Seguso Arte Vetro factory label on the lower body (see Marks & Labels). artworks.title: Green scavo glass horse with gold leaf
artworks.summary: A hot-sculpted horse in light green glass with a white, weathered scavo surface and patches of gold leaf on the shoulders and hindquarters. It stands with one foreleg raised and wears an applied collar. No signature or label has been found.
description: The horse stands on three legs with one foreleg raised and bent at the knee. The neck is high and arched and the head is large and expressive, with an open mouth, flared nostrils and a pointed ear in colourless glass. A stylised crest mane in ribbed sections runs down the neck, an applied collar circles the base of the neck, and a twisted tail hangs down behind. The horse is 28 cm high, 25 cm wide from nose to tail and 12 cm deep, and weighs 2.15 kg.

The glass is a light, transparent green with darker green flecks. Its surface is covered with an uneven white, chalky crust that gathers in the ribs of the mane, around the collar and along the tail, while the legs are smoother and glossier: a scavo finish, which imitates the weathered skin of glass recovered from the ground. Patches of gold-coloured leaf, most likely gold leaf, are laid on both shoulders and both hindquarters. No signature, engraving or label has been found.

The model is very close to a brown horse with gold patches that is recorded in an auction-results database under the name 'Ferro Murano' and dated there c. 1940–1949, and comparable to a dark green scavo horse that an American auction house offered in 2009 as probably by Alfredo Barbini (see Comparable examples). Both are attributions made by others for their own sales. Neither has been confirmed by a factory catalogue, a signature or a label, so neither is given here as the maker.

'Ferro' does not point to a single glassworks: several Murano firms carried the name, among them S.A.I.A.R. Ferro Toso and Barovier Seguso & Ferro, the firm that became Seguso Vetri d'Arte in 1937. The maker, the factory and the date of this horse are still being researched.

assertions.publicNote: No signature or label has been found. Auction records give two horses of very similar form to 'Ferro Murano' and, with a qualification, to Alfredo Barbini (see Comparable examples). Neither attribution has been confirmed, so neither is given as the maker of this horse.

Based on technique and comparison only: the scavo surface and applied gold leaf are Murano practices, and every comparable horse found so far is catalogued as Murano glass. There is no label or mark to confirm it.

evidence.locator: brown example, dated c. 1940–1949 in the record

assertions.publicNote: A working range, not a documented date. The only dated comparable is the brown horse recorded as c. 1940–1949, and that date has not been checked against a catalogue. Corroded and scavo-type surfaces appear on Murano from the late 1930s and became widespread after the Second World War, and green scavo horses with gold leaf are still made today, so a later production of this model cannot be ruled out.

artworks.title: Calcedonio shell bowl, signed Oscar Zanetti
artworks.summary: A heavy, asymmetric shell-shaped bowl in banded calcedonio glass, worked with clear glass at the rim and in pulled points around the sides. It is signed Oscar Zanetti in the glass and keeps its gold Zanetti Murano label.
description: A sculptural bowl in the form of an open shell, asymmetric and roughly heart-shaped seen from above. One side rises in a broad curled lip, the other narrows to a point, and small knobs of clear glass are pulled out around the sides like the spines of a shell. It is 31 cm long, 18 cm wide and 10.5 cm high, and weighs 3.28 kg, which makes it a substantial piece of solid glass for its size.

Inside, the calcedonio forms concentric bands of amber, olive, brown and purple that follow the hollow of the bowl, with lighter lavender and yellow streaks along the rim. On the outside the colours turn to grey-green and blue with fine white streaks. The thick clear glass of the rim and the points lets the bands show through in depth. As with every piece of calcedonio, the distribution of colour is unique to this example.

A cursive signature scratched into the glass on the underside is read as Oscar Zanetti, and a gold Zanetti Murano label with the firm's arched ZL monogram is fixed to the outer wall (see Marks & Labels). Together they point to Oscar Zanetti and the family furnace on Murano. The year of making and the model number have not yet been established.

A calcedonio shell of the same form in other colours has been offered online under Oscar Zanetti's name (see Comparable examples). If the comparison is confirmed, this bowl is one colourway of a model that the furnace made in several colours, as is usual for calcedonio.

marks.observation: Cursive signature in two lines, scratched into the glass with a hard point over the banded calcedonio. The strokes are frosted white and partly lost against the paler bands.
marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the owner's close-up photograph. With the letters upright, 'Zanetti' runs above 'Oscar'. The capital O and 'scar' are clear; the middle letters of 'Zanetti' are harder to make out.
marks.interpretation: The signature of Oscar Zanetti. It has not yet been compared with documented signatures, and the founder of the firm was also called Oscar, so it is not yet confirmed that this is the hand of the present master (b. 1961).

marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the photograph. The words are clear; the monogram under the arch is read as the letters Z and L.
marks.interpretation: Original label of the Zanetti furnace on Murano (Zanetti Murano). What the ZL monogram stands for, and in which years this label was used, has not been established; it may refer to Licio Zanetti, but that is not documented.

artworks.title: Calcedonio glass sculpture of a reclining couple
artworks.summary: A solid glass sculpture of a reclining couple, in colourless glass with flowing bands of calcedonio in blue, violet, red, amber and green. It is 38 cm long and carries an engraved signature that the owner identifies as Andrea Tagliapietra's.
description: A solid glass sculpture of two reclining figures, reduced to a few flowing volumes. The long body lies along the ground and tapers to a point at one end; at the other it rises steeply to two oval heads set side by side, one in banded calcedonio and one in colourless glass, with an arm forming a ring around them. A groove running along the upper surface lets the form be read as two figures lying close together.

Most of the volume is thick, colourless glass. Through it run bands of calcedonio, the marbled glass that imitates agate and other hardstones: blue, violet and red along the base, amber, yellow and green towards the pointed end, and a deep red in one of the heads. As the sculpture is turned, the bands shift and multiply in the clear glass. The surfaces are smooth and glossy.
The sculpture is 38 cm long, 17.5 cm high and 10 cm wide, and weighs 3.1 kg. A cursive signature is engraved on the underside, which the owner identifies as that of Andrea Tagliapietra (see Marks).

Both the subject and the handling match a calcedonio Lovers sold under Andrea Tagliapietra's name by the Franco Schiavon Gallery on Murano: the same simplified, fused bodies, one head colourless and one in calcedonio, and an arm ringing the shoulders. A sculpture catalogued at auction in 2026 as 'Lying Lovers' by him suggests a name for the model, but it is smaller and has not been shown to be the same model, so the name is used here only provisionally. When this sculpture was made has not yet been established.

marks.observation: A cursive signature scratched into the glass in thin, even lines, written quickly with long diagonal strokes, on a dark violet calcedonio area of the underside.
marks.transcriptionNote: Not transcribed letter by letter: several letters are not clearly legible.
marks.interpretation: Identified by the owner as the signature of Andrea Tagliapietra. It has not yet been compared with a documented signature by him.

assertions.publicNote: Based on three consistent indications: the engraved signature on the underside, which the owner identifies as Andrea Tagliapietra's; the calcedonio technique, for which he is known; and the close match in style with a calcedonio Lovers sold under his name (see Comparable examples). The signature is not clearly legible and has not yet been compared with a documented signature, so the attribution is not confirmed.
Follows from the attribution: Andrea Tagliapietra works on Murano. There is no label or 'Murano' mark on the sculpture.

No date is recorded on the sculpture and no dated example of this model has been found. If it is by Andrea Tagliapietra, it was made after 1979, when he became a maestro according to his gallery's biography. Related models are still offered today.
The opaque, marbled bands of blue, violet, red, amber and green set within thick colourless glass show the characteristics of calcedonio. The glass has not been analysed.

A sculpture catalogued at auction in 2026 as 'Lying Lovers' by Andrea Tagliapietra, and a related reclining couple sold by the Franco Schiavon Gallery as 'Lying lovers', suggest the name. Neither has been shown to be the same model as this sculpture, so the name is not used in its title.

artworks.title: Il Bacio (The Kiss), clear glass sculpture by Loredano Rosin
artworks.summary: A sculpture in solid clear glass of two figures, one bowing its large oval head towards the other. Loredano Rosin's own certificate of 1989 names it 'Il Bacio / The Kiss', no. 589. It stands 49 cm high on a black base engraved with his signature.
description: A sculpture of two figures in thick, colourless glass. A tall, upright figure, its body reduced to a rounded block with sloping shoulders, carries a large oval head on a narrow neck. Its face is indicated only by a long, straight nose and two narrow slits for closed eyes. The head is bowed towards a second, smaller figure that crouches close against the first, its rounded head lowered and its limbs drawn in beneath it.

Seen from different sides, the composition changes: from the front the crouching figure seems held in the arms of the upright one; from the sides the two are read as separate bodies, the one leaning over the other; from the back only the broad, rounded back and the oval head of the upright figure are seen. The glass is clear throughout, with smooth, polished surfaces in which the light gathers and bends.

The figures stand on a rectangular, glossy black base. On one side of the base the signature 'Loredano Rosin' is engraved in white cursive (see Marks). The sculpture is 49 cm high with the base, 24 cm wide and 28 cm deep.

A certificate of authenticity signed by Loredano Rosin and dated at Murano on 10 October 1989 belongs with the sculpture. In it he declares that the glass sculpture titled 'Il Bacio / The Kiss', no. 589, was made entirely by hand by himself, to his own design.

Couples are a recurring subject in his work. In the same catalogue Rosin writes that love and friendship, and couples in general, are recurrent themes, and that paired forms create the visual and emotional tension he looks for. Here the two figures are set close together, and the narrow space between them is part of the sculpture.

marks.observation: Cursive signature in one line, engraved into the glossy black surface of the base in a fine, dotted white line, as made by a fine engraving point. Capital L and R; the full first name is written out.
marks.transcriptionNote: Read from the owner's photographs. Both words are legible; the small letters in the middle of 'Loredano' are faint.
marks.interpretation: The signature of Loredano Rosin, on a sculpture documented by his own signed certificate. The full first name distinguishes it from works by his brother Dino Rosin. It is written more carefully and legibly than his quick pen signature on the certificate.

assertions.publicNote: Documented by the certificate of authenticity that belongs with the sculpture, in which Loredano Rosin declares that he made it entirely by hand to his own design, and signs. The signature engraved on the base agrees with it.
The certificate is issued at Murano-Venezia. There is no label or 'Murano' mark on the sculpture itself.
The certificate is dated 10 October 1989, so the sculpture was made by then. The year it was made is not stated.

assertions.statement: Solid colourless glass, shaped hot and polished
assertions.publicNote: The figures are modelled from thick masses of colourless glass with smooth, polished surfaces, the free-hand solid glass sculpture described in his catalogue. How much was shaped at the furnace and how much ground and polished afterwards has not been examined.

assertions.statement: Probably sold through the British trade around 1989
assertions.publicNote: Kept with the certificate and the catalogue is a 1989 letter from Murano Studio, a Murano glass dealer in Marylebone High Street, London, to its trade customers. The date on the certificate is written in English. Neither names the buyer, and the letter does not name the sculpture.

artworks.condition: A full condition report has not yet been made. The photographs show no obvious damage.

established: Sculpture of two figures in solid colourless glass, on a glossy black base.
Height 49 cm with the base, width 24 cm, depth 28 cm, measured by the owner.
The signature 'Loredano Rosin' is engraved in cursive on one side of the base.
A certificate signed by Loredano Rosin, dated Murano-Venezia 10 October 1989, names the sculpture 'Il Bacio / The Kiss', no. 589, made entirely by hand by him to his own design.
plausible: Sold through the British trade around 1989.
open: The year the sculpture was made.
What the number 589 counts, and whether it appears on the sculpture itself.
Whether The Kiss appears in his studio catalogue; no page showing it has been found yet.
What the base is made of, and whether the two figures are one piece of glass or two.
The weight, and a full condition report.
